I am 71 years old and have been working this land since I was sixteen. I never went to school, but I know my field like I know my own hands. My family has only 2.2 mu, and with my son working off-farm, it is mostly me and my wife who tend the crops. We cannot afford to take big risks — a bad year would hurt us badly — so I do what has worked before and what I see the neighbors doing.

This year I will plant chili on the whole 2.2 mu, same as last year. It is a good crop for our well water, and the dealers in town always buy it. I will prepare the soil with rotary tillage in early April, because that is what everyone around here does — it breaks up the ground nicely for the chili roots. For seed, I will buy an improved variety from the village supply shop. I have used the same type for a few years now. It is not the most expensive hybrid, but it gives steady results and I know how it grows.

I will put down about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu, mostly from compound fertilizer at planting and one top-dressing when the plants start flowering. I will also add about 15 kg of phosphorus and 18 kg of potassium per mu — I have learned that chili needs the potassium to set fruit well. I would rather use a little too much fertilizer than too little, because losing yield is worse than wasting a few yuan on extra bags.

We have a well, so I will irrigate five times through the season: once right after transplanting, then during flowering, and a few more times when the summer heat gets strong. I will spray pesticide about twelve times — aphids and mildew always come for the chili here, and if I skip even one spray I could lose half the crop. I do the spraying myself; hiring help costs money I do not have.

If the weather cooperates and I keep up with the watering and spraying, I expect to harvest around 5,000 kg per mu. That is what I usually get, and what my neighbors get when they do not cut corners.
